 Maxim Boldson

 In the final thirteenth segment of the Broken Silicon 386 podcast, the hosts discussed the gaming community's reaction to Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney's announcement that the recent dramatic performance boost and resource consumption reduction for the Epic Games Store launcher was achieved through the use of AI-powered generative programming (vibe coding). Many gamers, staunchly opposed to any artificial intelligence technology, harshly criticized the company for even mentioning neural networks. However, host Tom noted the inconsistency of this position: these same gamers are thrilled to be able to run unofficial ports of console exclusives like Bloodborne, created with AI tools, in 4K at 120 frames per second on PC. According to the podcast's hosts, unlike the pointless and expensive generated advertising from Coca-Cola, the use of AI to genuinely speed up slow software and save PC resources is an exceptionally positive example of the technology's application.
 The second major topic of the finale was rumors that the PC version of the blockbuster Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled for release as early as the first quarter of 2027—just a couple of months after the console release. Reporters believe that the publisher originally planned to release the PC version according to the standard schedule a year after the console release, but the rapid development of automated AI porting and hacking tools forced Rockstar Games to urgently shift the release schedule. From a traditional business perspective, it's advantageous for the company to keep silent about the PC version's existence until the last minute, to entice impatient players to buy the game twice—first for PlayStation 5 and Xbox consoles, and then on Steam.
 Nevertheless, Tom emphasized that if Rockstar tried to hide the information and announced the PC version only a month after the console launch, it would provoke colossal audience anger and push deceived users to download cracked pirated versions or unofficial AI ports en masse. According to the presenter, the company should act honestly and officially announce the game's PC release in early 2027, approximately two weeks before the console launch, immediately after the media frenzy surrounding the US elections subsides. In this case, PC gamers will calmly await the official Steam release, ignore pirated builds, and willingly pay $80 or $100 for a high-quality licensed product in which they will spend hundreds of hours.
